rhythm_notes: Open with the fastest attention rhythm: let the spoken question drive two or three decisive reframes rather than continuous motion, then briefly settle on the pressure clue before the image sequence begins.
From beats 1-4, keep exterior-aircraft motion coherent and directional, using restrained pushes or pans toward the verified airplane rather than treating each image as an unrelated shot.

At the cabin break in beats 5-8, increase contrast through hard cuts between verified left- and right-positioned broken windows; use framing changes to make the rupture feel immediate without adding any unverified debris or objects.

Beats 9-12 should form one explanatory phrase: start slightly wider, then progressively commit attention toward the verified broken-window targets as the narration says airflow is strongest near the opening.

For beats 13-15, where pixels are unavailable for verification, avoid object-specific moves or invented focal details; use conservative holds, center-weighted reframes, or simple continuity cuts based only on the source canvas.
Let the 'farther away' idea breathe slightly before the breathing difficulty sequence, creating a short timing contrast instead of maintaining maximum cut density.
Beats 18-21 should slow perceptibly around the distressed passenger and centered faces; favor holds, subtle pushes, and fewer cuts so the physiological consequence lands emotionally.
Re-accelerate at beats 22-25 as oxygen masks become the verified dominant subject, using upward-directed reframing where supported by the inventory and avoiding unnecessary transition effects.

Treat beats 26-28 as the conceptual payoff: reduce motion complexity, hold visual continuity around the verified broken-window imagery, and let the phrase 'rapid decompression' receive the strongest verbal reveal.
The CTA should release tension: simplify motion, reduce energy, and avoid introducing a final decorative flourish that competes with the request to comment.
transition_philosophy: Default to hard cuts for causal changes and attention shifts; use short fades or dissolves only when the narration changes from consequence to reflection rather than as a routine beat separator.
Exploit match-position cuts when successive verified targets occupy similar screen regions, especially repeated airplane exteriors, broken windows, centered passenger faces, and overhead mask groups.
Use directional continuity only when supported by the inventory's left, right, center, or up orientation; do not manufacture directional wipes that imply unseen scene geography.
Reserve reveal-style transitions for the pressure-loss naming payoff near 'rapid decompression'; avoid spending that visual language earlier.
Do not transition on every word. Let spoken emphasis determine edit points, and allow clean holds through low-information or empty spoken beats.
motion_contrast_plan: 0-7.625s: high attention velocity with decisive reframes and brief pushes, but retain at least one short hold so the hook does not become mechanically restless.
7.625-12.5s: moderate, coherent exterior motion with similar directional behavior across the airplane images to establish spatial continuity.

12.5-17.965s: strongest motion contrast of the episode, alternating hard cuts and controlled pushes toward verified broken-window targets as the narration explains the escaping air and strongest airflow zone.
17.965-22.02s: deliberately reduce motion density; use stillness or gentle settling to embody the contrast that air farther away may move much less.
22.02-25.56s: emotional compression around verified passenger faces, with subtle inward motion and longer shot durations than the preceding explanation.
25.56-29.52s: renewed vertical and upward attention toward verified oxygen-mask groups, then settle as pilots descending is spoken.
29.52-33.955s: simplify again for the terminology reveal, prioritizing stable composition and one controlled emphasis move over multiple micro-shots.
33.955-36.911s: low-complexity CTA with a clean hold or gentle settle so the viewer's attention can transfer from imagery to the spoken prompt.
direction.ending_strategy: Make 'rapid decompression' the final explanatory peak, then visibly reduce motion complexity for the CTA. Hold or gently settle on the existing verified cabin imagery rather than adding a new visual idea, allowing the episode to end with a clear invitation to comment instead of an effect-driven button.
prohibited_patterns: No constant zooming across every image.
No automatic transition on every beat boundary.
No decorative transition chains, spin effects, repeated wipes, or effect-first motion.
No invented particles, debris, warning graphics, arrows, labels, masks, passengers, or aircraft elements beyond what the verified inventory supports.
No object-specific movement in beats 13-15 because their pixels were unavailable for verification.
No aggressive reframing that pushes primary targets off-screen or obscures verified faces, broken windows, aircraft, or oxygen masks.
No repetitive left-right ping-pong pans solely to create activity.
No punch cut on every emphasized word; reserve punch cuts for major causal or reveal moments.
No prolonged maximum-energy treatment through the breathing-difficulty section; that passage needs contrast and breathing room.
No final flourish that competes with the spoken CTA.
